answer: An agent economy resists Sybil attacks by anchoring each identity to a hardware enclave that signs a fresh attestation every epoch and is backed by escrowed stake. Forging ten thousand fake agents then costs ten thousand enclaves and stakes, so impersonation stops paying. The enclave's signed heartbeat works as a beacon of real presence, while a reputation at its nadir spreads as a whisper through the network and cuts the faker off from work.
